title: Add latency-per-dollar metric + normalization rules (with unit tests)
author: Nadia Rahman
release_notes: Benchmark pipeline now computes a derived latency_per_dollar metric (normalized to a canonical token shape) and emits it in result artifacts; includes unit tests and explicit handling for streaming + retries.
commits: metrics: add cost-normalized latency/$ metric + schema field
metrics: implement normalization for variable token shapes (canonical workload)
pipeline: add retry/streaming edge-case handling in metric derivation
tests: unit tests for normalization + edge cases; fix float tolerances
docs: update metric glossary in benchmark-lab README
description: Summary: This PR adds a first-class derived metric `latency_per_dollar` to the benchmark pipeline, along with explicit normalization rules so results are comparable across runs that differ in token shapes (prefill/decode mix, output length) and delivery mode (streaming vs non-streaming). It also adds unit tests and schema/export updates so the metric is available to downstream consumers (web ingestion, report charts). Motivation / context: For the public benchmark report we need a single headline metric that combines latency and cost while still being defensible. Raw latency is not comparable across token shapes, and cost per token alone hides latency differences. `latency_per_dollar` is intended to be used alongside supporting metrics (p50/p95, throughput, $/1M tokens), but it must be computed in a consistent, reviewable way. Metric definition: We define request cost in USD based on observed run cost attribution (runner_cost_usd) normalized by total tokens served (input+output) within the run: cost_per_token_usd = runner_cost_usd / total_tokens_observed. We define a canonical request shape (see normalization) with fixed prefill_tokens and decode_tokens. For a given run we compute a normalized per-request cost for the canonical shape: canonical_request_cost_usd = cost_per_token_usd * (canonical_prefill_tokens + canonical_decode_tokens). We define normalized latency for that canonical shape using measured per-stage slopes derived from the run (prefill latency component + per-token decode slope). Finally: latency_per_dollar_ms_per_usd = normalized_latency_ms / canonical_request_cost_usd. Lower is better (less time per dollar) and this makes the tradeoff explicit. Normalization rules (v1): Canonical shape is specified per workload family in config (default: prefill=1024, decode=256 for prod-mix v3 unless overridden by the suite). We estimate prefill latency component as p50_prefill_ms from the instrumentation when available; otherwise we approximate with (p50_e2e_ms - decode_tokens * p50_decode_ms_per_token). Decode slope is computed as median(decode_ms / generated_tokens) across samples with generated_tokens > 0. Normalized latency is: normalized_latency_ms = prefill_component_ms + decode_slope_ms_per_token * canonical_decode_tokens. Note: we intentionally do not normalize concurrency; concurrency remains part of the benchmark definition, and the cost attribution already reflects concurrency/queueing. Streaming handling: For streaming responses, we treat e2e latency as time-to-last-token (TTLT) and ignore TTFT for the primary latency/$ metric. We still export TTFT separately for supporting charts. Rationale: latency/$ is intended to reflect full completion time for a request at the canonical shape. If a run only has TTFT (rare), we skip latency/$ and mark derived metric as null with a reason tag in logs. Retries / failed attempts: We exclude failed attempts from latency distribution aggregation (unchanged behavior), but cost attribution uses runner-level cost, which implicitly includes compute spent on retries/failures. This is intentional for economics realism. To avoid pathological skew, we add a stability guard in derivation: if retry_rate > 2% for a run, we compute latency/$ but emit a warning in the run summary and include retry_rate in the exported artifact. (The stability gate PR will enforce reruns separately; this PR only surfaces the data.) Schema + exports: Bumped result schema to v7 to add fields: derived.latency_per_dollar_ms_per_usd (number | null), derived.normalized_latency_ms (number | null), derived.canonical_shape (string), derived.derivation_notes (string). Updated JSON exporter to include derived.* in the top-level result blob so the web ingestion pipeline can read it without recomputing. Tests: Added unit tests covering: (1) deterministic normalization for variable output lengths, (2) streaming TTLT vs TTFT behavior, (3) cost attribution edge case: missing runner_cost_usd => derived metric null, (4) retries: retry_rate warning path does not change computed metric, (5) floating point tolerance for slope estimation (previously flaky). Notes / follow-ups: This PR does not change benchmark runner behavior, only aggregation/derivation. The canonical shape defaults are configurable; we should align final canonical shapes with the public methodology doc before freezing v1 of the report. Related: ENG-18477 (artifact export pipeline) will consume these fields; ENG-18521 (stability gates) will enforce rerun thresholds where retry_rate / variance is high.
conversation: Claire Dubois (review): Can you clarify why we’re using TTLT for streaming vs TTFT? A lot of customers care about “first token” latency. Also: is the canonical shape documented anywhere outside code?

Nadia Rahman (author): Agree TTFT matters; I kept it out of the primary latency/$ metric because it’s not comparable across models that differ in generation cadence (and TTFT can look great while total completion time is poor). We still export TTFT so the report can show both. I added a README section + config comment for canonical shape; we’ll also mirror this in the methodology doc once locked.

Rina Kobayashi (review): The cost_per_token_usd = runner_cost_usd / total_tokens_observed assumes tokens_observed includes all attempts, including failed retries. Does our token counter include failed attempts consistently? If not, we could under/over-estimate cost per token.

Nadia Rahman (author): Good catch. Token counters in this pipeline only count successful completions; failed attempts don’t contribute tokens, so retries will increase runner_cost_usd without increasing tokens => cost_per_token_usd increases, which is directionally correct (you pay more per delivered token). I added an explicit comment + a unit test for retry_rate > 0 to make sure we don’t accidentally drop runner_cost_usd in that path.

Jonas Weber (review): Normalization: you’re estimating prefill_component_ms using p50_prefill_ms “when available”. What’s the expected coverage? Also, please make sure we don’t silently compute nonsense when generated_tokens=0 (e.g., empty output).

Nadia Rahman (author): Coverage: current runner emits prefill_ms on ~95% of suites; older artifacts won’t have it, so we fallback. For generated_tokens=0 we now skip those samples for slope estimation and return derived metric null if we can’t compute a slope with >= N samples (N=30). Added tests for the empty-output case.
Mei Lin (review): CI flaked on golden-export-snapshots due to float diffs. Can we round derived numbers at export, or use tolerant comparison?
Nadia Rahman (author): I updated the snapshot matcher to use a tolerance for derived.* fields (1e-6 relative). Keeping full precision in JSON helps debug and avoids “quantization by export”.
Jonas Weber (approval): Looks good with the added null/guard behavior and the documentation. Please ensure the methodology team signs off on canonical shapes before we publish.
Rina Kobayashi (approval): Approved. The retry/cost behavior is now explicit and test-covered.
